headline: South Asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
- Asia: Ukraine pummels Moscow with drones on last day of Russian election.
- India: Iran threatens 'painful retaliation' if US strikes as Trump warns of 'big things'.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Residents dispute police’s shootout claim in Westmoreland man’s death.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Residents dispute police’s shootout claim in Westmoreland man’s death.
WESTERN BUREAU: Anger erupted in Seaford Town, Westmoreland, on Friday as residents reacted angrily to the death of 35-year-old businessman Jordon Perry Smith, who was killed in an alleged confrontation with the police about 3 a.m. While efforts to get an official version of the incident from the police were unsuccessful, a police source, who spoke to The Gleaner on condition of anonymity, said a targeted operation was carried out at Smith’s home.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russia threatens to further intensify attacks on Kyiv following hits in Moscow.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russia threatens to further intensify attacks on Kyiv following hits in Moscow.
Russia’s Defence Ministry threatened to increase strikes on military targets in Kyiv following reported Ukrainian drone and missile attacks on Moscow and Moscow Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russians attack Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast: five injured.
Russian forces attacked Dnipropetrovsk Oblast over 50 times with drones and artillery on 20 September, injuring five people and damaging homes in Nikopol.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian UAVs cause fire in warehouses and damage businesses in Kyiv Oblast – video.
Russian UAVs attack three districts in Kyiv Oblast, damaging company buildings and vehicles and causing warehouse fires in Boryspil district.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps deploys air-dropped kamikaze UGV for the first time during offensive in Donetsk Oblast.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps air-dropped kamikaze UGVs over 10 km behind Russian lines using bomber drones to liberate two villages in Donetsk Oblast.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russia’s secret plan to supercharge kamikaze drone production.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Russia’s secret plan to supercharge kamikaze drone production.
Documents obtained by POLITICO show a Russian state company blueprint for increasing drone carbon fiber production as the Kremlin escalates air war over Europe.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Merz vows to stay on as chancellor despite ‘disaster’ in another German regional vote.
The embattled chancellor’s conservative party suffered its worst result in postwar German history as the far-right AfD won its second regional election in two weeks.

Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran claims US preparing to resume attacks, threatens bases, supporting regional countries.
- Jerusalem Post, 9 hours ago: Iran claims US preparing to resume attacks, threatens bases, supporting regional countries.
The military said that any US attack would trigger sustained strikes on US bases and interests in the region, the report added.
- Jerusalem Post, 9 hours ago: 'No terrorist is immune,' Netanyahu says as IDF chief orders reinforcements to join manhunt.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir affirmed that should the terrorist who carried out the shooting attack is not killed during the manhunt, "he belongs on the gallows."
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: How will Saudi Arabia deal with the Houthis?.
Yemeni group warns of further attacks on the kingdom.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Man Utd salvage Fulham draw as pressure mounts on Carrick.
Matheus Cunha strikes late as Manchester United seal a 1-1 draw at Fulham, but pressure mounts on Michael Carrick.
Africa - bottom line: Gaza children return to school after years of war and displacement.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Gaza children return to school after years of war and displacement.
Children in Gaza are heading back to school as a new academic year begins, returning to classrooms that remain heavily damaged and lacking basic equipment after years of war.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
The United States on Sunday warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthis could “escalate rapidly” after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. “This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly,” the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”. US President Donald Trump also cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: Turkiye says it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs.
ANKARA: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia may have military needs due to the ongoing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis and that Turkiye was ready to help under a trilateral defence pact that includes Pakistan. “We see there are very serious attacks on Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity, sovereignty. We have an alliance agreement in our pact. We are in serious solidarity on this point. They may have some military needs, especially on some technical issues. We would have no issues in meeting these,” Fidan told broadcaster NTV.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Two officers among 6 martyred, 8 terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR.
Two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were killed in a fire exchange in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district on Sunday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. During an intense fire exchange between a “security forces convoy and Khwarij”, 23-year-old Captain Abuzar Farooq from Gujranwala and 22-year-old Lieutenant Sheraz Babar of Chakwal, “who were leading their troops from the front, fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom along with their four men”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Security forces kill 5 terrorists, recover 23 abductees in operation along N-25 highway near Balochistan's Kalat: ISPR.
Security forces have killed five terrorists and recovered 23 kidnapped individuals from their hideout during an operation along the N-25 Karachi-Chaman highway near Balochistan’s Kalat, the military’s media affairs wing said on Sunday. In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan tried to disrupt people’s movement by establishing a checkpost for abduction for ransom, extortion and snatching of vehicles along the N-25 highway, also knows as the Pakistan Expressway, on the night between Sept 18 and Sept 19.
Asia - bottom line: Ukraine pummels Moscow with drones on last day of Russian election.
- South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, Politico Europe, Taipei Times, just now: Ukraine pummels Moscow with drones on last day of Russian election.
Ukraine launched ⁠what Moscow’s mayor called the biggest ever drone attack on the Russian capital on Sunday, in what he said was an unsuccessful attempt to disrupt the final day of a parliamentary election that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for Russia’s war in Ukraine. The drone strikes killed two people in the Moscow region and two more in the Russian-held part of Ukraine’s Kherson region, including an election official, according to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin and...
- South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Russia vows revenge for Ukraine’s election-day attacks as poll shows win for ruling party.
Russia vowed on Sunday to “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv in response to Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow, as an exit poll showed the ruling United Russia party on course to win tightly controlled parliamentary elections. Ukraine fired waves of drones at Moscow and the surrounding region on the final day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze, officials said. Russia’s defence ministry accused Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens”...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Pacific island states are trapped in Cold War 2.0.
In early July, China fired a test missile from a nuclear submarine into the South Pacific for the first time, a weapon capable of carrying nuclear warheads. Washington and Canberra were livid. The Pacific has long been the exclusive testing ground for such long-range missiles from the United States. How dare China! The reaction from Pacific island states was more measured. While leaders from Tuvalu, Palau and the Solomon Islands strongly criticised the test, the 18-member Pacific Islands Forum...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Trump administration prepares sanctions against International Criminal Court, sources say.
US President Donald Trump’s administration has prepared sanctions against the entire International Criminal Court (ICC) and plans to announce them soon, two sources familiar with the matter said, ‌a move that would step up its attack on the global tribunal that prosecutes war crimes and genocide worldwide. The Trump administration has made no secret of its disdain for the court and has worked to undermine it. US officials want the court to drop its arrest warrants against Israeli leaders as well...
India - bottom line: Iran threatens 'painful retaliation' if US strikes as Trump warns of 'big things'.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Iran threatens 'painful retaliation' if US strikes as Trump warns of 'big things'.
Iran has reiterated its commitment to retaliate against the United States and its allies for any major offensive, citing credible intelligence indicating such actions are imminent. In response, President Donald Trump has issued a stern warning to Tehran about potential severe repercussions. The recent violence, including attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi sites, has aggravated tensions and disrupted regional energy supplies and maritime operations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: ‘Path of deception closed’: Iran vows ‘no limits’ in retaliation if US attacks.
Iran has issued a stern warning, promising unlimited retaliation and a decisive conflict if the US attacks or dismisses its demands. Through Qatari mediators, Tehran has proposed seven conditions for a truce to Washington. Officials in Iran stressed that any regional nations supporting the US would be drawn into the conflict. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf reiterated the dual approach of military readiness alongside diplomatic negotiations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: ‘When do I blow entire nation up?' Trump's ultimatum after Iran warns of 'decisive war'.
President Trump warned Iran of serious consequences if it does not change course. He outlined options including destruction, economic collapse, or diplomacy with Iran. Iran's command stated any US attack would face retaliation without limitations. Iran relayed truce conditions to the US through Qatari mediators. Trump signaled openness to talks with Iranian President Pezeshkian.
- Times of India - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: 'Could change a lot': Zelenskky and Trump to meet in New York ahead of UNGA.
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and US President Trump have agreed to a crucial meeting in New York, coinciding with the UN General Assembly. Zelenskyy thanked the US special envoys for their recent visit to Kyiv. During their discussion, the leaders emphasized the importance of security issues and outlined steps towards de-escalation, signaling a collaborative approach towards a stable future for Ukraine.
